summary: Navajo Nation lookout in Apache County, Arizona, on the Chuska Mountains; the register dates it to 2002, gives a probable 1960 build year, lists it standing; visits need tribal permission.

facts.design: 7-by-7-foot wooden cab on a 14-by-14-foot metal platform on a 12-foot tower (register description)

access.note: On Navajo Nation land. Tribal rules close all areas to non-Navajo visitors without a camping, hiking, or backcountry permit; no source read says who grants access to the tower itself.

events.note: Year given in parentheses in the register's description, not a Built field; probable, not confirmed

evidence.supports: one of the newest lookouts on the Navajo Reservation, with 1960 in parentheses
evidence.quote: One of the newest lookouts on the Navajo Reservation (1960)

evidence.supports: administered by the Navajo Indian Reservation

evidence.quote: The 7’x7’ wooden cab sits in the middle of a 14’x14’ metal platform on a 12’ tower.

evidence.supports: lookout already surrounded with electronic facilities
Roof Butte is the highest peak of the Chuska Mountains on the Arizona-New Mexico border
evidence.quote: Roof Butte is the highest peak of the Chuska Mountains which run in a north-northwest direction across the Arizona-New Mexico border.
The butte has an elevation of 9,787 feet (2,983 m)

evidence.supports: a staffed lookout tower is on Roof Butte
evidence.quote: A staffed-lookout tower is located on Roof Butte.
Roof Butte Apache 36.46083 -109.09592 Tower Standing NHLR US 440, AZ 36

evidence.supports: location on the Navajo Indian Reservation in Apache County
non-Navajo visitors need a valid camping, hiking, or backcountry permit from Navajo Parks and Recreation or another duly delegated tribal authority
evidence.quote: All areas on the Navajo Nation are closed to non-Navajos unless you have a valid camping, hiking, or backcountry permit issued by Navajo Parks and Recreation Department or other duly delegated tribal authority.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives the lookout site as 9,633 ft (2,936 m); Wikipedia gives the summit as 9,787 ft (2,983 m). The two figures probably describe different points, so the record keeps the register value.

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The 1960 date appears only in parentheses in the register description, so it is kept as a probable build year. The record's material 'steel' is not in the register text read, which describes a wooden cab on a metal platform; verify before keeping it. The register's 12-foot tower height looks low for a lookout at this elevation and may be a height above the platform; verify before using. Two web searches found no operator, fire history or visiting information. A search snippet attributed a 1960 date to an FFLA row, but the FFLA pages read do not show it, so it is not used. The Navajo Parks rules page was read; the permit page surfaced by search returned 404 and is not used.
